entries.name: osiris run
entries.description: Parses and executes an Osiris program with the tree-walking interpreter.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file, use `-f file`, or omit the path to read source from standard input.
entries.returns: process exit status and program output
entries.returnValue: Successful execution writes each `emit` value to standard output and exits with status `0`.
details: Parse, module, and runtime failures are reported as diagnostics and produce a nonzero exit status.

entries.name: osiris vm
entries.description: Compiles an Osiris program to bytecode and executes it with the virtual machine.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file, use `-f file`, or omit the path to read source from standard input.
entries.returns: process exit status and program output
entries.returnValue: Successful execution writes VM-produced `emit` values to standard output and exits with status `0`.
details: Use this command when checking interpreter and VM behavior against the same source.

entries.name: osiris eval
entries.description: Evaluates one Osiris expression without creating a source file.
entries.parameters: The remaining command-line text is parsed as one expression.
entries.returns: process exit status and one formatted value
entries.returnValue: The expression value is written to standard output on success.
details: Declarations and multi-statement programs belong in a source file passed to `osiris run` or `osiris vm`.

entries.name: osiris demo
entries.description: Runs the small demonstration program bundled into the CLI.
entries.parameters: This command accepts no arguments.
entries.returns: process exit status and demonstration output
entries.returnValue: The built-in program's emitted values are written to standard output.
details: The demo is a quick installation check; it is not a benchmark or a conformance suite.

entries.name: osiris debug
entries.description: Runs a source-level debugging session with optional breakpoints.
entries.parameters: Use `-break line[:column]` to add a source breakpoint and `-json` for machine-readable events. Pass a file or read source from standard input.
entries.returns: process exit status and debugger events
entries.returnValue: The command reports stops, source locations, and execution state until the program completes or the session ends.
details: Breakpoint lines are one-based; the optional column narrows the stop location.

entries.name: osiris repl
entries.description: Starts an interactive session that preserves bindings between inputs.
entries.parameters: This command accepts no arguments and reads expressions or statements from standard input.
entries.returns: process exit status and interactive values
entries.returnValue: Each completed input is evaluated in the persistent session until end-of-file or termination.
details: Use a source file for reproducible programs and the REPL for exploratory work.

entries.name: osiris fmt
entries.description: Formats source using the canonical Osiris layout.
entries.parameters: Pass a file or read from standard input. `-w` writes the formatted result back to the named file.
entries.returns: formatted source or process exit status
entries.returnValue: Without `-w`, formatted source is written to standard output.
details: A parse error prevents formatting and leaves an input file unchanged.

entries.name: osiris ir
entries.description: Prints the compiler's lowered intermediate representation.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Functions, blocks, instructions, operands, and terminators are written in deterministic order.
details: The output is an inspection format, not a stable serialized artifact contract.

entries.name: osiris ssa
entries.description: Prints static single-assignment form with explicit definitions and uses.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: The report shows renamed values and phi-like block flow produced by SSA construction.
details: Use this view to inspect optimization inputs rather than source-level formatting.

entries.name: osiris cfg
entries.description: Prints the program's control-flow graph.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Basic blocks and their successor edges are written in deterministic order.
details: The graph reflects lowered control flow, including branches and loop backedges.

entries.name: osiris dom
entries.description: Prints dominator information for the lowered control-flow graph.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: The report identifies each block's immediate dominator and dominator-tree relationships.
details: Dominance is computed from reachable control-flow blocks.

entries.name: osiris loop
entries.description: Reports canonical loop shapes discovered in lowered IR.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Headers, latches, exits, induction information, and proven trip counts are reported when available.
details: A missing fact is left unproven rather than guessed.

entries.name: osiris pure
entries.description: Analyzes functions and expressions for observable side effects.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: The report classifies analyzed code and records the effects that prevent a purity proof.
details: Unknown calls remain conservative and are not silently marked pure.

entries.name: osiris closure
entries.description: Shows closure conversion and captured environments.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Each closure and its captured bindings are written in stable source order.
details: The report distinguishes local bindings from values that must cross a function boundary.

entries.name: osiris infer
entries.description: Reports inferred value kinds, numeric widths, tensor shapes, and units.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Each inferred binding is printed with the most specific type information the analysis can prove.
details: Dynamic or incompatible facts remain unknown rather than receiving a speculative type.

entries.name: osiris alias
entries.description: Reports alias classes and escape information.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Bindings that may share storage or escape their defining scope are grouped conservatively.
details: Uncertain ownership is reported as possible aliasing rather than treated as independent storage.

entries.name: osiris viz
entries.description: Renders an abstract-syntax tree or import graph as Graphviz DOT.
entries.parameters: Pass `-imports` to select the import graph; otherwise the command renders the syntax tree. Source comes from a file or standard input.
entries.returnValue: The graph is written to standard output for inspection or piping into Graphviz.
details: Node and edge ordering is deterministic for stable diffs.

entries.name: osiris map
entries.description: Emits source-map information used by debugging and stepping tools.
entries.parameters: Pass one source file or omit it to read source from standard input.
entries.returnValue: Generated locations are associated with their original source spans.
details: Locations retain stable file, line, and column information.

entries.name: osiris c
entries.description: Lowers the supported native subset to readable C source.
entries.parameters: Use `-o` to write a file; otherwise generated C is written to standard output. Source comes from a file or standard input.
entries.returnValue: Unsupported native constructs fail during compilation with a source-aware diagnostic.
details: The backend lowers program behavior; it never runs the program at compile time to manufacture output.

entries.name: osiris obj
entries.description: Compiles native C lowering into an object file.
entries.parameters: `-o` names the required object output. Source comes from a file or standard input.
entries.returns: native object file and process exit status
entries.returnValue: The selected system C compiler produces the object file after successful Osiris lowering.
details: Compiler discovery and native feature limits match the other C-backend commands.

entries.name: osiris build
entries.description: Builds a native executable through the C backend.
entries.parameters: `-o` names the executable. Source comes from a file or standard input; native-cache and compiler options may further configure the build.
entries.returns: native executable and process exit status
entries.returnValue: The executable evaluates the lowered program when it runs.
details: Only programs fully supported by native lowering can be built.

entries.name: osiris compile
entries.description: Builds a native executable as an alias of `osiris build`.
entries.parameters: Accepts the same output, source, compiler, and cache options as `osiris build`.
entries.returns: native executable and process exit status
entries.returnValue: Its behavior and output are identical to the corresponding `osiris build` invocation.
details: Prefer `osiris build` in new scripts because it names the standard compilation path directly.

entries.name: osiris wasm
entries.description: Compiles the supported subset to a WebAssembly artifact.
entries.parameters: Use `-binary` for binary WebAssembly and `-o` for a file; the default output is WebAssembly text.
entries.returnValue: The artifact is written to the selected file or standard output after validation.
details: Unsupported operations are rejected instead of being replaced with interpreter output.

entries.name: osiris gpu
entries.description: Emits GPU kernel source or a machine-readable kernel plan.
entries.parameters: Use `-json` for a kernel plan and `-o` to select the destination file; otherwise source is written to standard output.
entries.returns: GPU kernel source or JSON plan
entries.returnValue: Supported kernels are emitted deterministically; unsupported programs produce a compile diagnostic.
details: The JSON form is for inspection and tooling; execution still requires an appropriate host GPU environment.

entries.name: osiris deps
entries.description: Reports resolved module dependencies and dependency cycles.
entries.parameters: Pass `-json` for machine-readable output and a source file or standard input as the dependency root.
entries.returnValue: Modules and edges are written in deterministic order; detected cycles are reported explicitly.
details: Resolution follows the same project, lock, cache, and version rules as program execution.

entries.name: osiris heap
entries.description: Inspects live scopes, modules, and dependency state.
entries.parameters: Use `-json` for structured output and `-query expression` to limit the inspected state. Source comes from a file or standard input.
entries.returnValue: The report describes reachable runtime state without changing the program.
details: Queries are inspection expressions, not arbitrary mutation hooks.

entries.name: osiris trace
entries.description: Executes a program while recording source-aware trace frames.
entries.parameters: Use `-json` for machine-readable frames. Pass a source file or read source from standard input.
entries.returns: execution trace and process exit status
entries.returnValue: Trace frames are emitted in execution order with their source locations.
details: Tracing preserves ordinary runtime errors and does not change program semantics.

entries.name: osiris help
entries.description: Prints the command catalog or concise help for one command.
entries.parameters: Omit the command name for the complete usage list, or pass one recognized command name.
entries.returns: help text and process exit status
entries.returnValue: Recognized help requests exit successfully; an unknown command name produces a usage error.
details: The short forms `-h` and `--help` print the top-level command list.
